seo.title: Factors of 30 Speed Grid - Number Theory & Divisors Game
seo.metaDescription: Find all 8 factors of 30 on a 100-tile math grid. Practice divisibility rules for 2, 3, and 5 in this fast-paced classroom math clicker.
seo.intro: Thirty is the product of three distinct prime numbers: 2 x 3 x 5. Because it combines three distinct prime building blocks, it has 8 factors: 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 10, 15, and 30. Searching for these factors across the 100-number grid teaches students to integrate multiple divisibility rules at once. Fluency Development: When students engage in timed identification on a 100-number grid, they move beyond manual finger-counting and transition into visual pattern synthesis. Developing automaticity with this specific math concept reduces cognitive load during multi-step problem solving, long division, and algebraic equation manipulation.
seo.howToPlay: Scan the grid to click all 8 factors of 30. Correct clicks highlight green with a checkmark. Non-factors flash red and cost 2 seconds of timer penalty. Locate all 8 factors to finish. Keyboard and Accessibility Controls: Students can use a touchscreen, trackpad, mouse, or keyboard arrow keys to navigate between tiles. Pressing Space or Enter activates the focused tile. Wrong clicks temporarily flash red with an X icon and subtract 2 seconds, but remain unlocked so learners can self-correct without getting stuck.
seo.teacherNotes: Highlight that 30 is divisible by 2, 3, and 5. This makes it an ideal case study for prime factorization trees (30 = 2 x 3 x 5). Classroom Implementation Ideas: Use this interactive grid during the first five minutes of math instruction as an energetic bell-ringer or daily warm-up. Teachers can project the screen onto an interactive whiteboard for whole-class competitive rounds, or assign the canonical link directly into Google Classroom for independent Chromebook math station rotations.

faq.q: What are the factor pairs of 30?
How does mastering click all factors of 30 support higher-level math standards?
faq.a: Building speed and accuracy with click all factors of 30 directly strengthens mental arithmetic and numerical reasoning. When foundational number facts become second nature, students can dedicate their active working memory to advanced problem-solving strategies, fraction equivalence, and multi-step word problems.
